We need to propose a retrosynthesis route with at least 5 reactions, using templates in order: ['29646', '1914389', '1914390', '149040', '1914391'].

We have applied first template 29646 to target, got three possible precursors (three branches). Need to choose one that can be further processed with next template 1914389, then 1914390, then 149040, then 1914391.

We attempted applying 1914389 to first precursor (with silyl group) and got a result (two products). That suggests 1914389 applied to that precursor yields two fragments: "C/C(=C/[C@H]1O[C@@H](CC=O)C[C@H](O)[C@H]1C)CO[Si](C)(C)C(C)(C)C" and "CCOC(=O)/C=C/CP(=O)(OCC)OCC". So the reaction splits the molecule into two pieces (maybe protecting group removal and ester formation). So after applying 1914389, we have two molecules.

Now we need to apply 1914390 to each? The order is fixed: after 1914389, we must apply 1914390 to the resulting molecules (maybe to one of them). We need to find a molecule among those that matches template 1914390.

We tried checking both candidates: first candidate didn't match, second also didn't. So maybe we need to choose a different branch from first template (the other two precursors) that will work with 1914389.

The three precursors from 29646 were:

1) "C/C(=C/[C@H]1O[C@@H](C/C=C/C=C/C(=O)O)C[C@H](O)[C@H]1C)CO[Si](C)(C)C(C)(C)C"
2) "C/C(=C/[C@H]1O[C@@H](C/C=C/C=C/C(=O)O[Si](C)(C)C(C)(C)C)C[C@H](O)[C@H]1C)CO"
3) "C/C(=C/[C@H]1O[C@@H](C/C=C/C=C/C(=O)O)C[C@H](O[Si](C)(C)C(C)(C)C)[C@H]1C)CO"

We applied 1914389 to first, got result. Maybe 1914389 can be applied to second or third as well. Let's test.
